---
title: Chapter one (already in the voice)
note: Written for the continuity tests; the section that precedes chapter two.
---

The patriarch Abraham rises early and saddles his donkey. He takes two of his young men and his son, and he splits the wood for the burnt-offering before he sets out. The text gives no word of his mind.

On the third day he lifts up his eyes and sees the place far off. He tells the young men to stay with the donkey. He lays the wood on his son and takes the fire and the knife in his own hand, and the two of them go on together.
